utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Will the registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may have the floor. Just a quick information for this Trial Chamber. My client, Mr. Milan Simic, was experiencing tremendous problems yesterday. First of all, their transportation came almost one hour later than the end of the trial; so it's 2.15. When he came to the UN, the other detainees have been in there having this, I don't know, walking out, so he was not able to get himself into the bed almost until 4.00 in the afternoon. He has these bedsores starting again, and again this morning because the guards are changing all the time, he is experiencing problems getting into this courtroom because of this platform. I mean, we are really -- he's doing his best and we're doing our best just to expedite this trial, but these things are really not going in this direction because what I'm afraid of is that things will go from bad to worse and then we are going to have to, I don't know, sort of adjourn for some time in order that he can recover. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It is important for you, counsel, to always bring these problems to the attention of the Chamber because the Chamber is aware of the medical condition and the health problems that your client is having. The Registry is doing everything possible, but these problems that you have brought to the attention of the Chamber will be looked into by the Registrar as well as the Detention Unit so that this is not repeated and the discomforts are not repeated to your client. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Prosecution is continuing. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: May the witness be shown Exhibit P12, please. It's the small map depicting the area in the vicinity of Bosanski Samac and adjoining municipalities, please. P12.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Mr. Lukac, can you see that map on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Do you know of a place called Batkovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of that place. MR. DI FAZIO: Could the usher just move it over briefly so that the town of Batkovic can be seen clearly?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: In the course of your incarceration, did you ever go there or were taken there at all or near it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not go there, but Batkovic is close to Bijeljina, where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. I've finished with P12. Yesterday, in your evidence, you described events that occurred in garage number 3. Did Stevan Todorovic participate in any beatings of either you or the people you were incarcerated with in garage number 3?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What sort of beatings?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday, I described the beating by Todorovic on Franjo Barukcic [redacted] while we were in the garage. However, he continuously beat prisoners, and this usually took place in the SUP building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How can you say that if you were incarcerated in garage number 3? What is your source of information?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted] [redacted]. Also, later on, when we were detained in the prison cells in the SUP building, we could hear quite well the beatings that were taking on, either in the hallway or in the duty room in the police station, and the voice of Mr. Todorovic could be heard very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday, you also described prisoners being brought into the SUP from time to time. Where were they housed in the SUP building? We've heard where you were housed, but what other areas, if any, were prisoners housed in the SUP?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These detainees were held in the offices; that is, on the premises adjoining the prison cells where we were held. And over a period of time, a number of prisoners were also kept in the basement of the SUP building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What information do you have as to the ethnic background of these prisoners?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All these men were of Croatian or Bosniak ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I now want to concentrate on the time when you were transferred from the garage number 3 into the cells. You've told us -- inside the SUP building. You've told us that you and Perkovic, I think, were put in one cell, that there was a cell next to you. Who was housed in that cell? A [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did that leave you alone in the cells, or did you still have a cell-mate?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the following period, that is, until I was exchanged on 4th of September, I remained alone in the cell and Mr. Barukcic remained alone in his cell and no other prisoner was brought and housed in those cells during that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Towards the end of July of 1992, was Mr. Todorovic still seen around the SUP building?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see him, but I heard his voice, which to me confirmed that he was present for periods of time in that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did he beat anyone, as far as you could tell?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The beatings that he carried out, and the other policemen did too. However, I think it may be important to say that in the initial stage of the war when these beatings were carried out by members of the special police who were stationed in Bosanski Samac but who had arrived from Serbia, now the beatings were carried out by the policemen from the Bosanski Samac area, which means that by now, they were adequately trained to perform such acts.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How can you comment that the local policemen were now engaging in beatings? What information to that effect do you have, or what did you observe that leads you to that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm led to that conclusion by the fact that these beatings took place on the premises of the police station on a daily basis. One could hear that very well in the cells where we were because it was very close, and I did see those policemen there either as guards in the police station or on the basis of their being in this building. I also received information to that effect from prisoners who were bringing in food for us or who communicated with us in some other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman named Antesa?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Antesa is really the man whose full name is Anto Brandic, and I knew him from before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was he imprisoned?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a while he was held in the office in the SUP building; that is, the police station, across from the hallway; that is, across from the prison cells where I was held. And from what I know, he was there for a couple of days, because I personally saw him when I went to go to the restroom, because we had to go out and walk down that hallway.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What fate did he meet?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that on the 29th of July, late in the evening, this man was taken out of this office to the room which is used by the duty officer at the station. He was beaten there by a number of persons, among whom was - I know this for sure - Mr. Stevan Todorovic, and the policeman Slavko Trivunovic. This beating went on for quite a long time in this room. And after he was beaten, he was taken out to the backyard of the police station where the beating continued. Then, to my knowledge, he was brought back to the office where he had been held and he died that same night from the consequences of this beating. That night, other prisoners were also beaten, a large number of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Could you hear what was going on from your position in the cell?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One can hear that quite well, especially his moans, because I assumed that he was being beaten very severely because of the loudness of his voice. I think that while he was being beaten in the backyard, half of the town could hear him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You mentioned in one of your answers just now a gentleman whose name is Slavko Trivunovic. Just tell the Chamber, did you know that man before the war, or did you come to find out who he was during your incarceration?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know that person before the war. He was a younger man, maybe 20 to 23 years of age. Based on information I received later, he was from a Serb village in the territory of Bosanski Samac. And while I was in the garage, I had an opportunity to see him in the backyard of the police station. Based on what I know, on the information I received from other prisoners after I had left detention, this -- he was a member of the Serbian police who was one of the men who was among those who mistreated people the most, and his specialty was pulling teeth out of their jaws with just common pliers. He would collect these teeth in a container and kept them as trophies.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What was his apparent function or duty or role at the SUP?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if he had any position, any commanding position in the -- within the Serbian police, but I know that he was a member of the Serbian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Would he frequent the police station, or was he just there from time to time on an apparently random basis?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how frequently he was there, but I did see him on that one occasion, and later on I could hear his voice quite often in -- on the premises of the police station in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: In the time that you were incarcerated in Bosanski Samac, either before were you taken away or upon your return, either in garage number 3 or in the cells, did you ever see, actually see, or speak to any men who had had their teeth pulled?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was there, I did not talk about it, but after I left the camp, I did, with a number of such persons, in fact. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I want to show the witness a number of photographs. I've had an opportunity of speaking to Defence counsel this morning regarding the problem of leading the witness by the appearance of the tab or label on the photograph. I've informed Defence, and they have unanimously, to the man, agreed that they have no objection to my showing the exhibit that's before the Court so long as yellow stickers have been placed over the English to avoid any leading of the witness. Court officers have very kindly done that. So I now want to show those photographs to the witness, and I don't think there will be any objections to my doing that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I see no objection. You can go ahead. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. May the witness be shown the bundle of photographs, Exhibit P9, I believe it is -- P14, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Now, the first photograph I wish to show you is F45 of P14. F45. First of all, what does that depict, Mr. Lukac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph depicts the building of police station in Bosanski Samac, and the photograph is taken from behind the building. This is the building. This is the wall that encompasses the backyard of the station. This is the building of the municipal building in Bosanski Samac. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. May the witness be shown F50 of P14, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What does that depict?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph depicts the complex of buildings of the Territorial Defence. This is the building where the prisoners were kept and this is the entrance gate to the compound. And by the way, this complex is directly across the street from the police station building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: When one was on the first floor of the police station looking out, is that the view one would have had?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One could see it very clearly from those windows.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. And there appear to be two doors, corrugated iron doors with crossed -- crossbeams cutting off the courtyard from the street. Do you see those doors?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were those doors the same doors -- I'll withdraw the question and rephrase it. In April 1992, were those doors in that position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you now look at photograph F51. Do you recognise that place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the duty room of the police station; that is, this is where the duty officer would sit while I was detained in the SUP building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were you ever interrogated in that room, or were you interrogated in other rooms about the building?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in this room.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Please look at photograph F52. What does that depict?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph shows the prison rooms in the Bosanski Samac station where I was for a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Just to be precise - I'm not clear from your answer - if they were the very cells about which you've given evidence of, namely, the cells in which you were incarcerated --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: -- which one were you kept in?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this one, the first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You see there's a window at the end of the corridor with criss-cross bars on it. What did that look out onto?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The window looks out onto the yard of the police station. But while we were there, these -- these windowpanes were not here but just the criss-cross bars. So this part had been removed, and only the bars were there. And these pieces of furniture here, the table and the chair, were not there. The corridor was completely empty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were the doors the same, the same mesh and metal doors?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Everything else was the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Please look at photograph F53. What does that depict?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph shows the yard of the police station. This is where the vehicles are. That's the yard. And this is the police station building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the photograph that I showed to you previously, the one depicting the two cells, had a window that you could see at the end of the corridor. I don't need to show it to you at the moment. Can you see the window that was depicted in F52 in F53?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. It's this window here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And would you please quickly have a look at F54? What do they depict?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph depicts the garages that are in the yard of the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And was garage number 3 in sequence? In other words, not visible in the photograph, but if you continue on to the left, you would have come to garage number 3?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here we can see only part of the door of that garage. This is it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Please go to photograph F55. I think my learned friends will [sic] object if I suggest that that must be garage -- room number 3 of the garage. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: It apparently depicts the interior of that room, and it's got a lot of clutter and stuff, objects in the room. What was the room like when you were actually imprisoned in room number 3 of the garage?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These objects were not there then. The garage was completely empty. And as I said, when we were brought in, there were only two outside tyres, car tyres there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What did you sleep on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We slept on the concrete floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How many of you were in there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were four of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: You said you slept on the concrete. What were the weather conditions like during the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in June. At that time, it rained very often, as far as I can remember, and it was very cold at night. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What did you have to cover yourself?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I explained earlier, we had a blanket. Two of us had one blanket, and the other two had a second blanket.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you have any sort of floor covering, a piece of cardboard or a foam mattress, anything at all, a piece of cloth?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, when we arrived, one of the policemen brought in a cardboard box which we laid flat on the floor, and we lay down on that cardboard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Please look at photograph F56 of P14. In the foreground -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Just one minute more. Now, imagine you're in this garage. What about air? Are those slats, or not, through which you get ventilation, that you see in the garage door there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That garage was covered with hardboard. The air was damp, but lack of air was not a problem, because these garages are not built of solid material, so they are not really hermetically closed. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Following on from His Honour's question, is that corrugated iron that makes up the doors?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay. F56, please. At the top of the photograph can be seen what seems to be a river. What river is that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The River Sava, the border between Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Republic of Croatia. This is it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And is that photo apparently taken from one of the upper floors of the SUP building?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Would you please look at photograph F65? What does that depict?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph depicts the door leading into the police station, which is entered from the street. This is it here. And then this is the corridor, and the corridor leading down the length of the building on the ground floor. And this is the staircase leading upstairs within the police station building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: If you stood on the ground floor that can be seen there, or the lower floor, and you walked down the corridor that you showed, the corridor that seems to lead underneath those stairs that you can see, would that take you to the cells in which you were imprisoned?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. And now finally, can you be shown photograph F67, please. Have you ever seen such insignia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen parts of this, the four S's, the Serbian colours, but I don't remember seeing this as a whole. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you very much. I've finished with the photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: From your cells in the SUP building, were you able to see out through that window that we saw in the photograph, into the backyard, at least partially?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you ever see cars, vehicles, in the yard?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What was happening in respect of those cars?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These cars were used by the Serb police to go about their business, the things they did at the time. Some of the cars were being repaired by a group of prisoners there, in the yard. They also washed the cars and did similar things.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Do you have any idea as to the origin of these cars, whose cars they were? I should say the ones being washed by prisoners and being repaired by prisoners.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were different vehicles there. Among them there was a number of vehicles which I assume were confiscated by force from citizens either in the town or on the roads in the Bosanski Samac municipality. One of these cars was mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Why do you make that assumption, that they were confiscated by force? What can you tell us that leads you to that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what leads me to this conclusion is the fact that a large number of the vehicles that turned up in that yard were civilian vehicles and had not belonged to the police before the war. On the other hand, very often members of the special police came to that yard. They were from Serbia, and as far as I could gather, the prisoners were repairing a number of vehicles for them, and I assume that some of these vehicles were subsequently taken to Serbia by these special policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman named Savo Cancarevic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Savo -- I know him. He was a policeman from before the war, and when Bosanski Samac was occupied, he became the commander of the Serb police force in the Bosanski Samac station.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you ever see him in the backyard?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you ever see him in the backyard when cars were there being repaired?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him. And I know that he addressed the prisoners who were repairing these vehicles. I think he asked about a certain vehicle. He wanted to know who it belonged to, and they replied that it belonged to one of the special policemen from Serbia. He then made a comment, and he said, "When they go back to Serbia, the only vehicles that will be left for us in Bosanski Samac will be bicycles."

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honour pleases, at this point I would like to play the 14 or -- it's about 14 minutes tape. It's the excerpts from the tape that was prepared by one of the Prosecutors in this -- who handled the matter before in the past, and the Defence have seen it. I think the result of yesterday's discussion was that they consent to its being depicted as long as there is no audio component to it, and I'm sure that the technical staff can make sure that it's simply removed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the number for it, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: These excerpts from the video depicting the areas around Bosanski Samac shall be marked for the record as Prosecutor's Exhibit P26. MR. DI FAZIO: Just for the sake of clarity for the technical room, the video has a label affixed to it starting with the word "Excerpts." It's got a number on it, V0003446. It is not the video -- the second video that should be in the technical room dealing with exchanges. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Just pause there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What's that building?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The photograph in this video shows the police station building in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Would you pause there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What does that depict?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What we can see here is part of the complex belonging to the Territorial Defence, the gate leading into the yard of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And just to either side of the gate that we discussed earlier from one of the photographs of two buildings, on the left-hand side of the gate there is a building with some sign above the window. You can see part of it there. Was that part of the TO?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That wasn't part of the TO. It was a shop which was in that building before the war. It was a shop for spare parts for cars, but the building belonged to the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. And what about the building on the right? Was that part of the TO?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Just pause there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What's that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the door leading into the Bosanski Samac police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Just pause there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: The camera went up some stairs. Which stairs are they?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are stairs leading from the ground floor of the police station building upstairs. Now we are upstairs on the first floor of that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: At the very end of the corridor is an open door and what seems to be an office. Whose office was that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the offers of the chief of police in which I worked before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Please pause there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: That's obviously panning around an office. Do you recognise the office?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is my office. Everything is the same as it was before the war except for one of those two telephones. It used to be green, and now I see it's red.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: If you look through those windows, it's not very clear in the film, but what would one see?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through this window, we can see the complex of the Territorial Defence buildings and part of the TO yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were you ever interrogated in that office?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These were the -- this was the conversation between the special policeman with the red beret. We were sitting here at this table.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Prior to the war, prior to April 1992, did you have a diploma, a piece of paper, or a document, a diploma?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had a diploma because I had graduated from university, and this was in the metal cupboard that you can see in this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have any idea where it was at the time that you were interrogated?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was brought into my office, I saw that the door of this metal safe had been broken open and my diploma had been torn up, and I could see pieces of it lying on the carpet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Just pause there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: It's just a tad late, but you saw what the camera panned over. Was that the TO?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a view from this office.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Just pause there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: That's obviously another office that seems to be attached to your former office. Whose office was that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the office used by the inspectors of crime-prevention unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Please continue

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Just hold it there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Again, can you see the TO from that window?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Through the window, you can see the yard of the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Just hold it there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: That -- the camera apparently left the second office and is now in a third office. Whose office is that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was also an office used by the inspectors of the crime-prevention unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Just hold it there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Is that part of a tree growing outside the SUP building?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't exactly recall, but I think, again, this is the view of the street and the yard of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: In the time that you were kept in the TO building initially, when you were arrested, did you know if those particular gates that you can see in the shot were kept open or closed, or have you no idea?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were kept detained. I had an opportunity to see that when I was taken out to the yard when we -- where we were beaten, or when I was taken to the -- to be questioned in the police station building. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm sorry, Your Honours, I missed the part of the transcript. Was it that they were kept detained or closed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm grateful to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I wonder, Mr. di Fazio, if we can find out what does it mean that the doors were kept detained. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, I'll clarify that. I'm grateful to Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you just tell us, were the -- I wasn't quite sure of your answer. Were the doors kept open or closed, as far as you were aware, in the period of time when you were in the TO building?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The gates were closed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: If we could return now to the video and please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The vehicles were not in the yard at that time. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ones we see inside.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I'd ask you just to have a look at that office. Perhaps we could pause there. Can you tell us what that office is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This should be the office of the chief of the police station, even though the chairs now are different from the ones that were there before, from what I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I may have misunderstood your evidence a little here, and I just want to be clear about it. The film showed earlier an office that you said was your office when you were chief of police. Is this also a chief of police office?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one that I referred to before was the office of the chief of the crime prevention unit, and this office is the office of the chief of the police station of Bosanski Samac, which means the number-one person, the overall chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I see. Thank you very much. MR. DI FAZIO: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Just pause there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Is that a view from the office that we have just seen depicted?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Just pause there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What does that tell you, that sign?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What it says is "Head of the Legal Administration Affairs." That means that it's the office of that official. At least, it was before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What floor is that on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is on the ground floor. When you go to the left down the hallway, first door to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier in your evidence that two women -- you noticed two women kept in custody. This is the occasion when you were made to sweep floors. Where were they kept in custody?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that very office.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Is this the office that you refer to where the two women were kept in custody?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Behind the door where you see the typewriter now, that is where they had their cots. MR. DI FAZIO: Just pause there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Who is that depicted in the poster?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The poster depicts the president of the Serbian Democratic Party during the war, Dr. Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Perhaps just stop there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You mentioned a man nicknamed Antesa. To your knowledge, was he ever in that room that we now see depicted?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is one of the offices where detainees were held, but from this image, I cannot say exactly, not from this particular frame.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Still holding it there, do you know how many people were kept in this room that we can see now? If you don't know how many, even an approximation, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number varied, so that in the office which is directly across from the prison cells and where Anto Brandic was held, there were about seven to eight persons kept there during one period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Just pause there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What's that room?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see now that the office that we saw before was the one where Anto Brandic was kept and this is the next one. This is where -- this is the service that does registration of motor vehicles. So citizens would come from outside, from off the street, where you see this person outside, and they would get that done.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were people kept in this room? Prisoners, I mean.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Again, do you have any idea of what sort of numbers were kept in this room?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Do you recognise that room? MR. DI FAZIO: If you could pause there as well, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise it. This is an office that was used by crime technicians before the war. A large number of detainees were kept in this office. While I was in the prison cell, this was the adjoining room. Again, at one point during one period of time, there were about 30 people kept there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thirty people in that room. About over what period of time were 30 people kept in that particular room?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That may have been July/August 1992. When Ante Savandic [phoen] was killed, that night people were brought out of that room and beaten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: What are the dimensions of this room like?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps 5 by 4 or 6 by 5 metres. I think those are probably the measurements. I cannot say exactly. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Do you have information as to the conditions under which those 30 people were kept? For example, bedding, food.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no beds. They were lying on the floor. And at that time, which means late June and July and August, the detainees were receiving one meal a day that was sometime around 1.00 p.m., and the meal consisted of a slice of bread spread with some jam and half a container of tea shared by two detainees.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How far away from that room were the two cells in which you and your friends were imprisoned? This is the period of time after you were taken away from garage number 3.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This office that we saw a moment ago is separated from the prison cells only by a wall. MR. DI FAZIO: Please continue with the film. [Videotape played]. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And while the film is running, if you look through those windows, is that a view into the backyard?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Just pause there, please. If we could just go back and get that last shot before the break, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Looking down that corridor, were your cells anywhere near that corridor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in this corridor immediately to the left, as seen from here. To the right is the office that we were referring to a moment ago where this man Brandic was held.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: So in effect, the cells you were in were across the corridor -- the doors to the cells that you were in were across the corridor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And if you -- it's a long corridor. As you look at the scene now, where were the doors to your cells, at the beginning of the shot, at the forefront of the corridor, or right down at the end of the corridor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the forefront. If you look at the crossbar of the bicycle, it would be on the opposite side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Just pause there, please. Perhaps just go back a little bit, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What does that depict?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This shot depicts the prison cells.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Is that the corridor that the camera is in?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was probably taken from the door, as you enter that room. MR. DI FAZIO: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Just pause there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Is that the interior of one of the cells?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: There seems to be some sort of makeshift bed. Was that there when you were in the cells?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In each of the cells, there is a -- there was a cot that was built there at the time when the whole cell block was built in 1987.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Please continue watching, Mr. Lukac, and pay particular attention to what's on the beds. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Pause there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: That's got a foam mattress on it. Did you have a foam mattress?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the cell where I was there, and no, there was no foam mattress. It was just the thing underneath.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What was the thing underneath? I can't tell. Is it solid or is it soft? What was it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a wooden cot, and it has a surface at the top which is not exactly hard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But of course, it is harder than this foam.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Sorry, and the dimensions of these two cells, the first one and the second one, are they about the same size? And if so, how large are they?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are identical in size. The length is the length of the cot, which probably means 2 -- 2.10 metres, and the width is perhaps 1.5 metres. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You said the length of the court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Cot. MR. DI FAZIO: Cot. I'm sorry. My apologies. I withdraw that. Yes, thank you. Please continue with the film.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Do you recognise this office? MR. DI FAZIO: Perhaps pause there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Just to be clear, the camera has now panned in to a second office. It panned in to a first office. Did you recognise that first office?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What was it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were offices in the -- on the lower floor. It will be to the right when you look from the front of the building. And what we are looking at now is the back office to the left, in that -- on that end of the corridor, and it was used by the deputy commander of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. The office that we -- is now depicted on the screen, were you ever interrogated in there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was interrogated there for the first time, and Mr. Stevan Todorovic was in that office at that time and the other individuals whom I mentioned on the first day. He was at the desk which can be seen here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was this the first interrogation that you underwent following your arrest?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the first interrogation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Please go ahead. Continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court where the camera is now going and what it is now depicting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The camera is showing part of the basement of the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were prisoners kept in the basement of the police station?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a period of time, yes, they were. And I assume that it was in this section here, past that metal door that we see. In which of these rooms exactly, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Could we just fast-forward now to the next scene? And if it could be played.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What does that depict?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were some of the rooms in the basement of the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Before the war, before April 1992, were prisoners kept there? I mean prisoners -- people who were arrested by police in the normal course of their duties.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's where the holding cells were until 1987. And then in 1987, new holding cells were built upstairs, where I showed you. And this was done in 1987. I remember this well. From then on until the beginning the war, the basement was not used for holding detainees.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Just pause there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Do you recognise that roadway?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This should be in the village of Gornja Crkvina. This is probably -- actually, no. This is the road from Bosanski Samac, the highway from Bosanski Samac via Doboj to Sarajevo. MR. DI FAZIO: Would you please continue.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: And pause here, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You've seen a bit more now. Can you tell us first the location of that roadway and the buildings you've just seen.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The road that can be seen is the highway that I referred to, that is, the Bosanski Samac-Doboj-Sarajevo highway. This is the village of Gornja Crkvina, and the building we see here is the youth centre and other structures that were -- and the building we see to the extreme left, that is where I was held the first three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You said you were arrested in Crkvina, and your evidence is -- was it somewhere near to this place that's depicted, the point at which you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was arrested, and I think that if it -- if we roll the tape more, I think we can get to the exact location.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I think it's finished there. If we could just rewind briefly to that last scene and the white buildings depicted in it. You said in evidence that you were kept in a youth centre. I just want to be absolutely clear about that. Where is it shown in this particular shot?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the rooms in which I was detained the first three days is in the building to the far left. You can see those two windows there. And what you can see in the middle of this picture, this big building, that is the youth centre building in the village of Gornja Crkvina. Behind the main building there is a hall. And as far as I know - and I found this out later, after I was released from camp - Croats from the neighbouring Croatian villages which were occupied after the war were brought there, and they were held in that hall or gym. And after that, they were separated off and taken to other camps in Bosanski Samac or in the village of Zasavica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, it's slightly after our break time. MR. DI FAZIO: And I've finished with the tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. All right. So that's the end with the tape. MR. DI FAZIO: That's the end of tape, the end of the use that I want to make of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So can we take our break and resume the proceedings at 1130 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecutor, please. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What was the date on which you were exchanged, Mr. Lukac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 4th of September, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: The last few weeks before that exchange took place, were you beaten at all?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And just to be absolutely clear, in the last few weeks before the exchange, you spent your time in the cells in the SUP building?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And Franjo Barukcic was still in prison with you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He remained with me, and he was exchanged at the same time as I was, on the 4th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: When did you first become aware of exchanges taking place, the fact of exchanges, the phenomenon of exchanges?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we were taken from Batajnica to Bosanski Samac, Fadil Topcagic, who came to collect us, told us that he had come to take us to be exchanged. However, after our arrival in Samac, after we were locked up in the garages we talked about earlier, no one mentioned an exchange to us anymore. In the following months, we did get some information that some people from the camp were being exchanged, and we ascertained that exchanges did exist [redacted] [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Throughout your evidence, you've described people that you were incarcerated with following your arrest and their ethnic background. I want you to think back now on all of the places that you were imprisoned, right up until your exchange, and tell us -- comment upon another aspect or quality of the prisoners. Were any of them combatants or soldiers, as far as you could tell, people who were imprisoned with you, covering the whole -- from Bosanski Samac to Brcko, to Bijeljina, Batajnica, back in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was detained on the 17th of April, 1992. I was arrested at 10.30 a.m. and locked up in the village of Gornja Crkvina. Three days later, I was transferred to the TO warehouse in Bosanski Samac. On the 26th of April, in the evening hours, I was transferred to the prison of the JNA barracks in Brcko, where I remained until the 2nd of May, 1992. On the 2nd of May, 1992, I was transferred from the JNA prison in the Brcko barracks to the Bijeljina barracks. On the 3rd of May, 1992, I was transferred from Bijeljina to the military prison in Batajnica. On the 12th of May, 1992, I was transferred from Batajnica to the military prison in Zemun. On the 15th of May, I was transferred from Zemun back to Batajnica. On the 26th or 27th, I was transferred from Batajnica to Bosanski Samac again. That was when I was taken to that garage. I think it was the 23rd of June that we were transferred to the prison cells in the police station. We remained there until the evening of the 3rd of September. At about 23 hours, we were transferred from there to the gym of the primary school in Bosanski Samac. And on the following morning, the 4th of September, 1992, we were exchanged. Together with me in the cells where I was kept, there was not a single soldier taken prisoner at the front line during the military conflict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before you leave this description, which of those places where were you taken to after your arrest were in Serbia, if any?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I did not understand your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I was asking from the date of your arrest until your release, all these places where you were taken to, was there any place which is actually in Serbia, and which ones are those?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand now. There were two places in Serbia where I was detained, and those are Batajnica and Zemun.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You obviously became aware of the possibility of exchange and exchange taking place. Did you seek to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On one occasion when we were in the prison cells in the police station building, we were visited by a delegation - I might call it that - headed by Svetozar Vasovic. He said that he was working in the Serbian Red Cross in Bosanski Samac, and he asked the four of us if we wanted to be exchanged. Of course we said we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever see the method by which prisoners who were in custody were chosen for exchange? I'm not talking about how the exchange actually worked but how the prisoners might be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what method was used to select the people who were exchanged, but I do know that these exchanges were used to commit ethnic cleansing of Croats and Bosniaks from that area, because mostly it was civilians from that area who were exchanged. And when I was exchanged, I had an opportunity to convince myself that this was actually the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I want to turn to the night of the 3rd of September, the night before your exchange. How were you first informed that it was about to take place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember all the details, but I think it was in the early evening that one of the Serbian policemen came into our detention area, and he told me and Mr. Barukcic that an exchange was to be organised the following day and that the two of us were on the list of people to be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you speak to anyone that night in the SUP, apart from Franjo Barukcic, about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Yes. Please tell us.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At around before 2000 hours on that evening, the duty officer arrived. He took me out of the cell. He took me upstairs to the police offices that we saw of the crime prevention unit that we saw in the video, and then a number of my colleagues who used to work in the crime prevention unit talked to me. They had worked with me before the war in the crime prevention unit. These were all inspectors of Serbian nationality. Until the outbreak of the war, I had been their chief. In fact, they had summoned me upstairs to say goodbye to me because they knew there was going to be an exchange, and that's why they summoned me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman named Milos Savic? Milos Savic. I apologise for the pronunciation.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. Milos Savic is an inspector, or he was an inspector of the crime prevention unit before the war. He worked with me. I was his chief. And during the war, he was an inspector in the crime prevention police unit in that Serbian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was he anywhere on this occasion when the inspectors said goodbye to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean that conversation that evening?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was one of the people in that office.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did he say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me that he was sorry about everything that had happened to me and that -- because he knew everything that had been done to me, to me and to other people, that he was ashamed to be a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you remain in the -- remain in the cell, prison cells, in the SUP that night?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We remained in the cell until about 23 hours, as far as I can recall, and then we were taken out, Mr. Barukcic and I, and we were taken by truck to the gym of the primary school in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What was -- what did you observe at the gym?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we were brought into the gym, it was completely dark inside because there was no electricity at the time. The gym was full of people. There were women and men. There was a large number of people inside. I think that they had been brought in that night from different locations, and they were Croats and Bosniaks to be exchanged on the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Elderly people?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of them were elderly people, although there were also others.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was there anything about their condition, their physical condition, their clothes, things they had with them, that indicated to you whether or not these people had been prisoners?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was able to observe this only on the following morning when dawn broke, when we were being taken for exchange in the bus. Then I noticed that among all those people who were on the bus - and I think there were about 70 or 80 people there because the bus was full - there were seven or eight prisoners whom I knew had been in camp, because a number of them I could recognise. I knew them because they had been with me from the beginning in imprisonment. And the other reason I recognised them was that their heads were shaved, completely shaved, but not all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Now, you've just described coming into contact with an extra 70 or 80 people. Was there anything about them that allows you to comment on whether or not they were combatants, soldiers, military types?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, in that bus, the people who were exchanged on that occasion, none of them was a combatant.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You -- I want to turn now to the trip to the exchange point. You've mentioned buses. Did you go -- were the people who were to be exchanged placed on the buses and transported on the buses?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were all put into that bus in front of the building, the primary school in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How many buses?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, there was only one bus, and it was full.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was there any escort to this bus?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a police escort. There was a police vehicle in front with uniformed policemen inside. Behind them, there was a civilian vehicle in which Mr. Miro Tadic sat, Svetozar Vasovic, and Veljo Maslic also. Behind that vehicle was the bus, and behind the bus there was another police vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: To be absolutely clear, the gentleman you referred to as Mr. Miro Tadic, is that one of the defendants in this case, Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How long did the trip take to the final exchange point?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The trip lasted for quite a long time, because before the exchange, we had been taken to a town called Bosanska Gradiska, which is quite far from Bosanski Samac. How long it took exactly, I couldn't say, but it was several hours. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown the Times map, please. Can it be placed on the easel. I'm not quite sure of the exhibit number. I'll be able to provide it to the Chamber in a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What was the number? Okay. I understand it is P15. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm grateful to the Chamber. Thank you. If it could be placed on the easel. And it's just behind me over here, against the wall. It's behind the usher where it will not fall down. May I just approach the map briefly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Mr. Lukac, can you just go to the map --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would be very grateful if our learned colleague will just explain us what he pointed out just now with his right finger. MR. DI FAZIO: I can inform the Chamber that I pointed to a town in -- I wasn't conscious of actually pointing. I can only recall looking at a town. But if I did point - of course I trust Mr. Pantelic's observations completely - I pointed to the town of Bosanska Gradiska.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In front of a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The point is that the town of Bosanska Gradiska is as it appears on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That is correct, Madam President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But the proper way as I see this procedure is if I would be my learned colleague Mr. Gramsci di Fazio, I would go to the map, without pointing anything, check where is the town, and then I go back. So that would be the proper way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm absolutely sure that Mr. Lukac is perfectly aware where is Bosanska Gradiska, but it's rather a matter of principle of the behaviour of our learned colleagues. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think it was an oversight. I don't think we need to do it. If we can proceed on other matters. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Just point out firstly, Mr. Lukac, if you can, firstly the town of Bosanski Samac on the map. It's a long distance between the easel and the bench. And then if you can, if you can locate it, with or without prompting, the town of Bosanska Gradiska.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you indicate Bosanska Gradiska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bosanska Gradiska is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: So it's to the west, along the northern border of Bosnia and Croatia.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. You can sit down now. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the map be left there just in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Now, you told us you stopped in Bosanska Gradiska. What did you do there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you repeat your question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I'm sorry. You told us that you stopped in Bosanska Gradiska. What did you do there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bus on which we were came to a stop somewhere. I had never before been in Bosanska Gradiska, but I think that it was in the centre of town. For a long period of time, I think three, four, or five hours, we sat there waiting. I think that they were probably discussing the procedure of the exchange itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Eventually did the convoy continue?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While we were waiting there, I know that another four buses loaded with people to be exchanged arrived, and later I learned that these were people from the territory of Doboj municipality. And if I can recall, about 1730 hours, they crossed the river -- the bridge on the River Sava at Bosanska Gradiska over to the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Where were you exchanged?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The exchange took place at the gas station which was damaged, I assume, by fighting, and this was the village of Dragalic, which is by the Slavonski Brod-Zagreb highway.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: About how far from Bosanska Gradiska would this village be?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how far it was, but I would say some 10 to 15 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So does that mean you were actually taken into Croatia, or was this still B and H?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were taken to Croatia. But the area across from River Sava, across from Bosanska Gradiska, was under the control of Serbian rebels in Croatia. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Pre-April 1992 was it Croatia territory?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Is it now part of Croatian territory?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I want to play a portion of a videotape that I have referred to.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. Just one correction. You asked whether that territory was in the Republic of Croatia prior to April 1992. The territory, as I said, was controlled by the Serbian rebels in the Republic of Croatia since 1991, since the outbreak of hostilities there, and that part of -- that region is called Western Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Prior to the outbreak of hostilities in general in the former Yugoslavia, was it part of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN LUKAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Would Your Honours just bear with me while I gather now the transcripts of the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. I have copies of the transcript available with the case manager here. The video itself is also with the -- in the technical room, and it's ready to go. Before I play it though --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: How long is it? MR. DI FAZIO: The video itself is quite long. It's over an hour. I only want to refer to certain portions of the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. So just certain portions. MR. DI FAZIO: Certain portions of it. It can be played again at a later stage. And with this witness, I only need to play certain portions of it, and I just want to draw your attention to certain parts of the transcript so that it will make it easier for the Chamber and for Defence counsel to follow the brief parts that I want to draw the Court's attention to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the number for the video footage and the transcript, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This video shall be marked for the record as Prosecutor's Exhibit P27, and the transcript shall be marked for the record as Prosecutor's Exhibit P27A, and the B/C/S version shall be marked for the record as Prosecutor's Exhibit P27A ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Is this -- Mr. di Fazio, is this a video on the exchange of prisoners? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Perhaps, then, the exhibit could be marked accordingly "Exchange of Prisoners." MR. DI FAZIO: I would be grateful if that could be done. There are just some matters that I want to draw the Chamber's attention to in relation to the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can go ahead. MR. DI FAZIO: You see at the top of the page, there are numbers. You should have two documents. At the bottom of the page, you'll see, "Text in German." If you turn to the additional translation that I've provided, at the very top of that page is the numbers 02908.
